newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Deutsche Bank sees progress on SES listing.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bank sees progress on SES listing.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank AG said it might offer part of its 4.24 percent holding in Luxembourg satellite company Societe Europeenne des Satellites SA (SES) in a listing operation for SES.

"We are facing an important step: bourse listing... hopefully in the not too distant future. We could make part of our holding available," Ekkehard Storck, managing director of Deutsche Bank Luxembourg SA told a news conference on Wednesday.
His remarks had been embargoed for publication on Friday.
Deutsche Bank, which helped found SES, holds its SES stake through DB Lux.
Storck said the listing plans would "advance in the course of the year."
Deutsche Bank AG board member and outgoing DB Lux supervisory board chairman Ulrich Weiss said SES had been a successful investment for Deutsche Bank.
SES, which had a 1996 net profit of 233 million marks, is European market leader in satellite transmission.
Through its European Satellite Multimedia Services joint venture with companies including Intel of the U.S. it is also active in the multimedia field.
Storck gave no indications how SES's other shareholders might act in an initial public offering.

SES said earlier this week the earnings growth was partly due to income from the Astra 1E and 1F satellites which started service in 1996. Turnover rose by 37 percent to 14.06 billion Luxembourg francs last year.
SES invested 13.30 billion francs to build new satellites and ground control systems in 1996. Four satellites are currently under construction for launch in 1997 and 1998.
